tutorial.title: Exception Handling Best Practices
tutorial.descriptionContent: Handle expected failures without hiding unexpected problems.
tutorial.shortDescriptionContent: Python learners who can handle multiple exception types and messages

lessons.title: A misleading error report
lessons.interactiveContent:
A try block should focus only on the code that might cause the error we want to handle. This keeps error handling clear and predictable.

In the example below, there is a lot of stuff in the try block. Let's change that!

lessons.title: Find the risky operation
lessons.interactiveContent:
To keep the try block focused, we must first identify which lines can cause errors.

Here, order["quantity"] can fail if "quantity" isn’t a key, and int() can fail if its value isn’t a valid integer.

Make sure to pick int, followed by "quantity".

lessons.title: Focus the try block
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we put only the code with expected failures inside try, other errors won’t be caught by mistake.

Make sure to pick try, followed by except.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If we put only the code with expected failures inside try, other errors won’t be caught by mistake.

Handle the quantity conversion, then reduce the total by the discount outside the handler.

Make sure to pick try, followed by except, and finally -.

lessons.title: Focus the try block - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
And if we expect specific errors, we can add a separate except handler for each one. This makes it even clearer what error is occurring.

First check for KeyError, then for ValueError.

Make sure to pick try followed by except and then KeyError, except, ValueError.
lessons.hardModeContent:
And if we expect specific errors, we can add a separate except handler for each one. This makes it even clearer what error is occurring.

First handle a missing quantity key, then invalid integer text. Match each handler to its printed response.

Make sure to pick try, followed by except, KeyError, except, and finally ValueError.

lessons.title: Choose a useful boundary
lessons.interactiveContent:
A handling boundary is the place that knows what to do after a failure.

parse_quantity() converts a value. process_order() knows which order to skip and what message to show.

Make sure to pick except, followed by ValueError, and finally return.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A handling boundary is the place that knows what to do after a failure.

parse_quantity() converts a value. process_order() knows which order to skip and what message to show.

Store a valid quantity. For invalid text, stop this order without raising another error.

Make sure to pick =, followed by except, ValueError, and finally return.

lessons.title: Recover where context exists
lessons.interactiveContent:
parse_quantity() lets ValueError travel to its caller because it can't choose an order-level response.

process_order() catches it because that function can stop one order and explain the failure.

Make sure to pick except followed by ValueError and then print, "Skip order: invalid quantity".
lessons.hardModeContent:
parse_quantity() lets ValueError travel to its caller because it can't choose an order-level response.

process_order() catches it because that function can stop one order and explain the failure.

On invalid quantity text, display Skip order: invalid quantity without requesting input.

Make sure to pick except, followed by ValueError, print, and finally "Skip order: invalid quantity".

lessons.title: Recover where context exists - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We don’t need to catch every possible error. Within a specific function, we should focus on the expected errors.

If any other error pops up, the code that calls this function should handle it. That's why we don't add a general except block.

Make sure to pick except ValueError:.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We don’t need to catch every possible error. Within a specific function, we should focus on the expected errors.

If any other error pops up, the code that calls this function should handle it. That's why we don't add a general except block.

Make sure to pick =, followed by except.

lessons.title: Leave other work outside
lessons.interactiveContent:
Some things that might fail but are not our concern can and should be called outside a try block.

Call calculate_total() after the handler so a failure in that separate operation stays visible, and we don't catch it.

Make sure to pick calculate_tota.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Some things that might fail but are not our concern can and should be called outside a try block.

Calculate and store the total after the handler so a failure in that separate operation stays visible.

Make sure to pick =, followed by calculate_total.

lessons.interactiveContent:
start_server() can stop startup and explain a bad port. Complete its handler around parse_port().

Make sure to pick try, followed by except, and finally ValueError.
lessons.hardModeContent:

lessons.interactiveContent:
Add exception handling around the call inside process_order(), where the program can skip one order.

Make sure to pick try, followed by except, and finally ValueError.
lessons.hardModeContent:

Make sure to pick try, followed by "quantity", except, and finally ValueError.

lessons.title: Complete a focused handler
lessons.interactiveContent:
A cart importer receives quantity text. Invalid quantities should be skipped, while valid items should be saved. What should the code do?

Catch only ValueError when converting the quantityCatch every possible errorSave the item before converting the quantity

Catch only ValueError when converting the quantity.

lessons.title: Make the next step clear
lessons.interactiveContent:
Handling an error keeps the program running, but a printed message may never reach the user or other code.

Clear fallback values like None make failures visible to the parts of the program that need to respond.

Make sure to pick return, followed by None.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Handling an error keeps the program running, but a printed message may never reach the user or other code.

Clear fallback values like None make failures visible to the parts of the program that need to respond.

Display An error occurred: with the details, then return the failure value without requesting input.

Make sure to pick print, followed by return, and finally None.

lessons.title: Return a clear sentinel
lessons.interactiveContent:
Returning None makes errors easier to respond to because the rest of the program can tell when something went wrong.

Unlike a simple print() statement, a fallback value lets other parts of the program detect and respond to the failure.

Make sure to pick return, followed by None.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Returning None makes errors easier to respond to because the rest of the program can tell when something went wrong.

Unlike a simple print() statement, a fallback value lets other parts of the program detect and respond to the failure.

Make sure to pick except, followed by return, and finally None.

lessons.title: Return a clear sentinel - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Returning None makes errors easier to respond to because the rest of the program can tell when something went wrong.

Return None if the code runs into an error.

Make sure to type None.

lessons.title: Name the fallback result
lessons.interactiveContent:
The caller can check the fallback value to see whether the operation succeeded or failed.

Check if the response from parse_quantity() is None.

Make sure to pick if, followed by is, and finally None.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The caller can check the fallback value to see whether the operation succeeded or failed.

Use is to check for None. Pass invalid integer text so the caller prints Order skipped.

Make sure to pick "two", followed by if, is, and finally None.

lessons.title: Use a default deliberately
lessons.interactiveContent:
A default is useful only when it's a valid result. A discount of 0 safely means no discount. That's better than None in some cases.

But using 0 for an invalid quantity would invent an order value, so that case needs a different fallback.

Make sure to pick 0.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A default is useful only when it's a valid result. A discount of 0 safely means no discount. That's better than None in some cases.

But using 0 for an invalid quantity would invent an order value, so that case needs a different fallback.

Make sure to pick ValueError, followed by 0.

lessons.title: Silence hides failures
lessons.interactiveContent:
The pass statement lets us handle an error without running any code.

A bare except with pass hides every failure. The caller can't tell why the function returned 0.

Make sure to pick pass.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The pass statement lets us handle an error without running any code.

Catching every failure without a response hides its cause. The caller cannot tell why the function returned 0.

Make sure to pick except:, followed by pass.

lessons.title: Catch the expected error
lessons.interactiveContent:
Silent handlers also hide unexpected bugs that the program can't recover from meaningfully.

Catch ValueError, the failure expected from int(). Other failures remain visible.

Make sure to pick except, followed by ValueError.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Silent handlers also hide unexpected bugs that the program can't recover from meaningfully.

Catch invalid integer text. Return the no-discount default while leaving other failures visible.

Make sure to pick except, followed by ValueError, and finally 0.

lessons.title: Pair handler and fallback
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the fallback with an explicit return.

Make sure to pick return None.
lessons.hardModeContent:

Make sure to pick return, followed by None.

lessons.title: Choose a useful fallback
lessons.interactiveContent:
A missing quantity means an order can't be processed. Which fallback makes that result explicit without inventing a quantity?

return Nonereturn 0

return None.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A missing quantity means an order can't be processed. Which fallback makes that result explicit without inventing a quantity?

return Nonereturn 0return ""

Make sure to pick return None.

lessons.interactiveContent:
Which handler catches the anticipated conversion failure and gives the caller a clear fallback?

`except ValueError:
return None``except:
pass`

Which handler returns a clear failure value and catches only that conversion error?

except ValueError: return Noneexcept: passexcept ValueError: return 0

except ValueError: return None.
